sections.h2: What is the Callaway County Recorder of Deeds responsible for?
sections.html:
Land transactions in the county are kept on public record by this office, and a house sale in Callaway County is not finished until the deed is filed with it. The county's Recorder page says the office handles deeds, deeds of trust, releases, easements, surveys, plats, affidavits, marriage licenses, military discharges and tax liens.

Christine Kleindienst holds the office. The office is open to public research and keeps transactions in historical order. A seller usually never walks in, since the title company sends the deed over after closing. It still helps to know what the office will and will not accept, because a rejected deed can hold up your payoff.

Homeowners in the Kingdom of Callaway who are considering a fast sale for cash should know the recorded deed is the final step. Cash Home Buyers can explain what the title company will request from the recorder ahead of closing.

sections.h2: Where do I find the Callaway County Recorder?
sections.html:
It is in the Historic Courthouse in Fulton, the county seat, and the county lists the details below.

  • Address: 10 E. 5th Street, Fulton, MO 65251
  • Telephone: 573-642-0787
  • Fax: 573-642-1491
  • Hours: opens at 8:00 in the morning, staff stay until 4:30 in the afternoon, and the register shuts at 4:00 (this schedule began July 17, 2023)

The 4:00 register cutoff matters on a closing day. A deed handed over at 4:15 will most likely be recorded the following business day, so find out from the title company which day it plans to submit. The same courthouse holds the Collector, Assessor and County Clerk, which makes one trip enough for most questions about a property.

sections.h2: What should a Fulton-area seller know about Callaway County?
sections.html:
Callaway County sits north of the Missouri River, across from Jefferson City, and covers about 835 square miles of land. Wikipedia describes the northern part as flat with few large forests, while the southern edge along the river is heavily forested hills and valleys. Cedar Creek forms most of the western border. Statistically it belongs to the Jefferson City metro area, and Fulton serves as the seat.

Missouri organized Callaway on November 25, 1820, with Elizabeth as its first seat. It is also called the Kingdom of Callaway, a nickname from the Civil War era when local leaders arranged a ceasefire with Union troops. German immigrants who arrived from the 1830s on planted the vineyards that later returned as wineries. The Callaway Nuclear Generating Station stands near Fulton.

Incorporated places here are Auxvasse, Fulton, Holts Summit, Mokane and New Bloomfield, with part of Jefferson City on the south side. Public school districts that reach into the county include Fulton 58, North Callaway County R-I, South Callaway County R-II, New Bloomfield R-III, Community R-VI and Jefferson City Public Schools, so look at which one appears on your tax bill before you list.

sections.h2: What will recording my deed cost in Callaway County?
sections.html:
The state statute lets the recorder keep $5 on page one and $3 on every page that follows. A flat $2 statewide increase under Senate Bill 938 started on August 28, 2026. The bill at the counter runs well above $5, since other statutory fees ride along on each instrument.

For comparison, Cole County's published schedule charges $26 for a standard first page plus $3 per added page, and Camden County posts the same pair. Call the Callaway Recorder at 573-642-0787 and ask for the fee sheet in force today. Other charges in RSMo 59.310 include:

  • $5 for each extra item when one document releases or assigns more than one item
  • $25 extra when a document does not meet the format rules
  • $1 for a certificate and seal, and up to $2 for the first copied page plus $1 for later pages
  • $25 per sheet to record a subdivision plat, and $5 per sheet for a survey of one or more tracts

Nothing in that fee list is priced from the sale amount, so a deed is billed by pages and document type. The title company totals the recording charge on your settlement statement.

sections.h2: What format must a deed have to be recorded in Callaway County?
sections.html:
RSMo 59.310 lets the Recorder turn away any document that fails its layout rules, so whoever drafts your deed must follow them. The core requirements are brief.

  • Paper is white or pale, twenty-pound stock or heavier, printed single-sided and left unbound.
  • Print runs at eight point or larger in dark ink and must copy cleanly.
  • Page one leaves a blank three-inch strip at the top for the recorder's stamp, with three-fourths of an inch clear on every other edge.
  • Each signature is inked dark and sits above a typed or stamped name.

Under that blank strip, page one has to carry the document title and date, each grantor with marital status, each grantee, required addresses and the legal description. A document that misses these rules can still go on record for an extra $25. Older deeds signed before 2002, certified copies and papers executed abroad escape the format rules altogether.

A rejected document comes back to the person who submitted it with a written reason, so a mistake costs time more than money.

sections.h2: How do I search Callaway County land records?
sections.html:
You can view recorded documents online at callawaymo.icounty.com. The Recorder's page says printing is available through subscriptions at several levels, and you can call the office for the options. The page also points to DeedWatch, a notification service run by the county's records vendor, which can alert an owner whenever a new document is filed under that name.

That alert is useful for a seller who has inherited a house or who shares a title with a relative, because it shows a lien, a release or a new deed soon after it is filed. It can also surface a filing you did not expect before a buyer's title company finds it.

The county also offers free GIS maps for the public, listed on its home page, which help with parcel lines on rural lots outside Fulton.

sections.h2: Which other Callaway County offices matter when I sell?
sections.html:
Three more offices share the courthouse at 10 E. 5th Street. The Collector's page gives their weekday hours as 8 to 4:30, closed on state holidays.

  • The Collector, Sarah Gladman, at 573-642-0747, bills and takes property tax payments. Per the county FAQ, statements are mailed during the final week of October.
  • The Assessor, Jody Paschal, values more than 26,000 parcels. Real property calls go to 573-642-0768, and personal property to 573-642-0766.
  • The County Clerk handles Board of Equalization appeals.

The Assessor's own page says field crews gather data in marked vehicles, wear safety vests with body cameras and county ID, and knock first. They take outside photos, may ask about a finished basement or the number of bathrooms, and never ask to come inside. State law puts the Board of Equalization filing cutoff on the second Monday of July. The Assessor's 2026 notice named July 8 at 5 p.m. instead, so ask the Clerk each year for the date that applies.

Back taxes or an open lien on the house should go to the title company early, so the payoff appears on the first draft of the settlement.

faqs.q: Where is a Callaway County deed filed?
faqs.a: At the Recorder of Deeds, 10 E. 5th Street, Fulton, MO 65251. The register closes at 4:00 in the afternoon. Call 573-642-0787 to ask how to submit it.

faqs.q: What is the Callaway County recording fee?
faqs.a: The statute sets $5 and $3 as the recorder's base, other statutory fees are added, and a $2 statewide increase began August 28, 2026. Cole and Camden Counties post $26 for page one, so request the current Callaway sheet.

faqs.q: Can I look up a Callaway County deed online?
faqs.a: Yes. Recorded documents can be viewed at callawaymo.icounty.com, and the Recorder sells subscriptions if you want to print them. The office can also explain what each level includes.

faqs.q: Why would the Recorder reject my deed?
faqs.a: The usual reasons are format problems under RSMo 59.310: a margin smaller than three inches at the top of page one, small or faint type, signatures without printed names, or missing grantor and grantee details. The office sends the document back with a written reason.

faqs.q: Is there a Callaway County transfer tax?
faqs.a: The fee list in RSMo 59.310 carries no transfer tax, only charges by page and document type. Confirm the total for your own deed with the Recorder at 573-642-0787 or with your title company.
